newsitem.title: UK: Dollar charts buzzing with bullish signals.
newsitem.headline: Dollar charts buzzing with bullish signals.

text.p: Dollar charts are brimming with positive signals for further gains, and pullbacks will only help to provide it with gunpowder for an extension of its sizzling rally, technical analysts said.

The dollar has gained some four percent against the yen and three percent versus the mark over the past week. It pushed to its highest level in over four years just shy of 127 yen overnight. Against the mark it is keeping up the pressure for a test of its 1997 high against the mark at 1.7210 marks soon.
"The dollar's bull run shows no real signs of abating. It is very well supported, and the focus remains clearly on the upside technically," said Alan Dunne, chartist at Bank of America.
Dollar/yen has led the dollar rally after its break through a key psychological hurdle at 125 yen Monday.
Now many chartists are pencilling in 130 as the next target, a far cry from the record low around 79.75 it hit two years ago this month. The next immediate target is 128.35, the July 1992 top.
At 1108 GMT the dollar was at 126.24/34 yen and 1.7153/59 marks, up from 126.00/05 and 1.7112/18 in late European trading on Tuesday.

Historically 130 is not much of a level, neither as support nor as resistance. The key barrier to watch is 129.50/60, an area marking a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the entire five-year decline from 160.35 in April 1990 to the record low.

"The dollar uptrend is intact as long as it holds 124, which has to remain in place for a move to the next upside target at 128.20/40," said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at CSFB.
A break above the dollar's 1997 high at 1.7210 marks, and more crucially the 1.7230/55 highs of March and April 1994, would open up a target at 1.7686, the 1994 peak.
Critical levels on the downside to negate the bullish long-term bias are far away, providing the dollar with a big cushion on downticks.
Only a break below 1.6610 marks, the bottom of the curent range, and the December uptrend at 124 yen, would spark a technical sell-off, chartists said.

Part of dollar/yen's fortunes are dependent on the mark/yen cross though, which looks technically weak. "I'm a little less bullish on dollar/yen than on dollar/mark because of mark/yen," said Dunne at Bank of America.
Stiff resistance above 74 yen is weighing on the mark, with resistance around 74.20/25, the six-week highs of late March ahead of an eight-year old trendline around 74.60/65 seen difficult to crack.
A sell-off of the cross would boost the yen and also weigh on dollar/yen. Mark/yen was at 73.61/62 versus 73.65/68 at the previous European close.
Andrew Chaveriat, technical analyst at Banque Paribas in New York, pointed to the "April effect" on dollar/yen.

"The April effect reveals that frequently over the past decade, dollar declines accelerate, or dollar rallies stall during April," said Chaveriat. He expects the upswing to end next month after a rise towards 128.85.

Against the mark, a break below support at 1.7090 would open up a potential double-top, but the bearish signal generated from such a chart pattern would only be confirmed on a move below 1.6615, the seven-week trough from late March, said Bank of America's Dunne.
Despite the dollar's gains against the mark, analysts caution that much of its firing power comes from mark weakness rather than independent dollar strength.
Just as against the mark, the dollar has yet to exceed its 1997 highs from early March against the French franc, the Italian lira and the Swiss franc.
